scope_fields.approach: Exact coordinate-row lifting, compactness-to-leakage implication, and accumulation of coefficient losses
proved_deductions: The quotient essential-normality premise is equivalent to vanishing degreewise squared adjoint leakage.
The restricted coordinate-row squared inverse norm is exactly (1-epsilon_n)^(-1).
One fixed finite homogeneous generating family, including lower-degree bases, has product-energy bounds given by a finite product of these inverse factors.
Essential normality yields subexponential degree-dependent product-energy bounds for that family.
Summable squared leakage gives degree-uniform stable division for that family.
For the principal radical ideal (z_1), the coefficient product grows linearly although the true product-energy stable constant is one.
An explicit pair generating a prime infinite-codimensional ideal is unstable, but a single redundant generator repairs the entire displayed witness sequence.
not_proved: The stable-division converse under compactness alone.
An ideal lacking every finite homogeneous stable generating family.
Essential normality of the additional prime-ideal calibration example.
Stable division for every element using the enlarged family in the prime-ideal calibration example.
Novelty of any elementary deduction in this report.
prior_work_credited: Kennedy arXiv:1202.1797v2 Theorem 3.8: stable generating family if and only if closed algebraic sum of principal Hilbert submodules.
Shalit arXiv:1003.0502v2: stable division definition, forward essential normality theorem, known positive cases, and Example 2.6 quantifier warning.
OWR15/2023 p850: reported Kennedy-Shamovich angle characterization.
